draft.title: Staying safe online
card: Cyber safety means protecting yourself and your information when you use the internet. Personal details include your full name, address, birth date and passwords.
Keep personal details private. A strong password is long and hard to guess, and it is not shared or reused on every account.
A scam tries to trick you into giving away money or details. Warning signs include a deal that seems too good to be true, pressure to act fast, and messages from strangers asking for details.
A fake shop looks real but takes payment and sends nothing. Before paying, check that the site address starts with https and shows a padlock, and use a secure payment method.
draft.remember: Guard your details, use strong passwords, spot warning signs and pay only on secure sites.

a.why: A long mix of words, numbers and symbols is hard to guess. The others are short or use common words, names or dates that others could guess easily.
a.clue: Which one would be hardest for someone else to guess?

b.q: Leo finds a website selling a new phone at half the usual price. A banner says the deal ends in 10 minutes. What is the best thing for Leo to do?
opts: Stop and check the site for warning signs first
Pay quickly so he does not miss the deal
Send his birth date so the site can confirm him
Share the link with friends and then pay
b.why: A very low price and pressure to act fast are warning signs of a scam or fake shop. Leo should stop and check the site before paying. Paying quickly is tempting, but it is what a scammer wants him to do.
b.clue: Which warning signs does the offer show?

b.best: Stop and check the site for warning signs first

problems.detail: The card presents https and a padlock as a check against fake shops. Many scam and fake shop sites use https and show a padlock. The padlock only means the connection is encrypted, not that the shop is real (Scamwatch makes this point). Students could take a padlock as proof a shop is genuine. Add that a padlock alone does not mean a shop is real.
"It is not shared or reused on every account" suggests reusing a password on some accounts is fine. Reword to say a strong password is not shared and is not reused across accounts.

check.summary: Both questions are sound. The card implies that https and a padlock show a shop is safe, which fake shops often have too, and its password advice wrongly suggests reusing a password on some accounts is fine.
